messages:
arjun: morning handoff from me -> nina. i'm primary until 18:00 UTC, mike is secondary for the next 12h. i'm out for a meeting 14:30-15:15 UTC, coverage gap noted.

arjun: quick status: all services green, 99th latency for text-gen is 210ms last hour, no rate-limit spikes. no active incidents.

nina: thanks — noted. are there any ongoing customer-impact watchers?

arjun: none. outstanding follow-ups: infra team is tracking a spiky disk IO pattern on ded7, but no errors surfaced so far. ticket #INF-447.

susan: ping re: paging matrix — can you confirm who to page for P0s on hosted api? last doc had a stale contact.

arjun: sure. updated matrix below (also added to runbook):

<pagerduty-bot>: Incident policy: "Redwood - Hosting P0" -> Primary on-call (api-hosting) -> Escalate to Secondary after 5m -> Escalate to Eng Lead after 12m -> Exec on-call after 30m.

arjun: practical steps:
1) P0 (service down / customer-impacting error rate > 50%): page primary via PagerDuty immediately using the PD webhook or `pd incident create` -> if no ack within 5 minutes, PD auto-esc to secondary -> after 12 minutes, page eng-leads.
2) P1 (degraded perf / partial impact): slack @oncall first, create a PD incident but mark severity P1, give 15m to respond.
3) P2 (non-urgent regression): create ticket in JIRA and notify secondary during overlap.

mike: small clarification — for region-specific outages (e.g., eu-west), page regional on-call first (api-hosting-eu) before global primary, escalate to global after 7m. added to runbook.

nina: during my planned swap at 18:00 UTC, if arjun hasn't handed off, what's expected?
susan: standard: person logging out should post a short handoff in this thread, mention any active watchers, and transfer ownership in PagerDuty. if not, secondary must assume primary at shift boundary and announce.

arjun: exact PD commands we use in runbook:
```
# create P0 incident
pd incident create --service "Redwood - Hosting P0" --urgency high --title "P0: Hosting API outage" --body "Start triage: <link to logs>"
# escalate manually (if needed)
pd incident escalate <incident-id> --to user mikesmith
```

susan: runbook links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-handoff, https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paging-matrix, https://redwood.internal/playbooks/hosted-api-p0.

mike: quick triage checklist (short):
- check /health on the service: `curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/health`
- check pods: `kubectl get pods -n hosting -o wide`
- check CPU / GPU utilization and queued requests in the runtime dashboard
- if KV cache thrash suspected, enable fallback-cache via console route override (see runbook).

nina: coverage gap note: between 14:30-15:15 UTC arjun is in a meeting. mike — can you be reachable in that window? if not, confirm a temp swap now.

mike: i can cover 14:30-15:15. i'll be reachable by phone and slack.

oncall-bot: Reminder: weekly maintenance window tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC. Any on-call conflicts? react with :white_check_mark: to acknowledge.

arjun: small change to paging rules for noisy alerts: do not page for single 5xx spike < 1% of traffic. require a sustained error rate > 5m and > 3% before escalating to P1. this reduces noisy wakeups. documented in paging-matrix.

susan: escalation contacts (quick):
- Primary on-call: api-hosting (PagerDuty service) -> contact via PD (calls/sms)
- Secondary on-call: api-hosting-backup
- Eng leads: arjun, susan (pager duty users: arjun, susan)
- SRE manager: mike

mike: if PD fails, fallback is manual Slack @channel mention in #eng-oncall + call the on-call phone list (listed in runbook).

nina: thanks all. i'll post a short handoff sticky at 17:55 UTC with any last-minute notes. posting checklist: active watchers, PD incidents IDs, outstanding tickets, temporary overrides.

arjun: final note on customer comms: only send statuspage updates for confirmed customer-impacting incidents (P0/P1) and coordinate with comms. use the statuspage template in playbooks.

nina: acknowledged. grabbing handoff now. :white_check_mark:
